Rebecca Whiting

Libertarian candidate for U.S. Senator, Minnesota · Open seat

Farmer; owner of Dirty Goat Farm & Bakery (Bemidji)

Rebecca Whiting is a U.S. Army veteran who served as a combat medic in Iraq. She is a farmer and small business owner in Bemidji and chairs the Libertarian Party of Minnesota. She won the Libertarian primary on August 11, 2026, and is on the November 3, 2026 ballot as the Libertarian candidate for U.S. Senate.

Where Whiting stands

Federal spending and national debt
Wants the U.S. to erase the national debt, cut taxes, and deregulate business. Her campaign says overspending and printing money have caused inflation.
Foreign policy and war
Supports non-interventionism. She says the U.S. war with Iran repeats the mistakes of Iraq and Afghanistan, and her campaign opposes wars fought without a declaration of war.
Health care
Supports privatizing the VA, arguing that free-market providers would give veterans faster access to care.
Abortion
Her campaign describes her as the only pro-life candidate on Minnesota's U.S. Senate ballot.
Debate access
Objects to MPR limiting its debates to major-party candidates and calls for third-party candidates to be included.

Background

  • U.S. Army, 7 years; combat medic in Iraq (Ramadi 2004–05; Baghdad 2006–07, 2ID, 2BCT)
  • Farmer and owner of Dirty Goat Farm & Bakery, Bemidji
  • Chair, Libertarian Party of Minnesota
  • Board member, Bemidji's Natural Choice Farmers Market
  • Won Libertarian primary for U.S. Senate, August 11, 2026
